label: D1 reward-gated reset: up after reward (esp. rare S1), down after loss late; a2-history drift
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_common == 0) * (prev_state == S1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_common == 0) * (prev_state == S1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S2) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) ;; ((tv("action", -1) == 2) + (tv("action", -2) == 2) + (tv("action", -3) == 2) + (phase == D2) * (action == 2)) * ep_trial * (phase != D1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_state == S2)
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 24 (timing alone R^2 0.71; rises strongly late in the episode, highest at D1). Beyond timing, the magnitude is mainly set at D1 by the previous outcome shown: higher after a rewarded trial (+0.11), especially after a rare-rewarded a2->S1 trial (+0.12 more), and lower after unrewarded trials, with the loss-related drop growing with the trial index in the episode (-0.0019 per trial), so late in the episode reward vs no reward splits D1 widely. After a1->S2 (rare) trials D1 is lower (-0.06); after a rare a2->S1 loss it is a bit higher (+0.06). At GO it is higher after a previous a2 choice (+0.04), at D2 higher when S2 is reached (+0.05), and at GO/D2 it drifts up with the number of recent a2 choices times episode trial (an episode-level a2-preference build-up seen in the worst windows). All terms use only observed variables (the action at D2 is already made). Dev R^2 beyond timing 0.80, test 0.80, matching the all ceiling 0.80 (last-trial table alone 0.73). The hidden good state, since-reversal and value add little.

issues: The score reproduces (test 0.8048). But the term set has no D1 constant, so the fit has to use the win indicator and the loss x ep_trial term to stand in for one. Adding a single (phase == D1) term and replacing the loss x ep_trial term with a plain D1 loss indicator raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.805 to 0.847. That is well above the claimed 'all' ceiling of 0.80, so 'same as the ceiling' does not mean nothing is left to explain.

The claim that the loss drop grows with episode trial ('-0.0019 per trial', 'late in the episode a win and a loss give very different D1 values') does not hold up. Once a D1 constant is in, the loss x ep_trial weight falls to -0.0005 and test R^2 drops slightly (0.8437 vs 0.8469 with plain loss/win indicators). A win x ep_trial or win x late-ramp term adds nothing either (0.841-0.843). The win-loss gap at D1 is a roughly constant +0.24, not '+0.11'.

The 'x ep_trial' build-up in the recent-a2-count term is not supported. Without the ep_trial factor it scores the same (test 0.80486 vs 0.80476). So 'creeps up with recent a2 choices times episode trial; a build-up across the episode' overclaims.

The a1->S2 effect at D1 shrinks from -0.064 to -0.042 once a D1 constant is in. A plain (phase == D1)*(prev_state == S2) term does slightly better (test 0.850), so the a1-specific claim is not needed.

The parts that hold up: rare a2->S1 rewarded gives an extra boost (dropping it costs 0.26 of R^2), the gate is higher at D2 when S2 is reached and at GO after an a2 choice, and the rare a2->S1 loss is less negative. The worst-fit windows are late-episode (t87-99) under-predictions across all phases. After the fix, misses show only small residual cells (at most about 0.04, e.g. GO after a1 S2 r +0.038, GO after a2 S1 r -0.034). Adding the model's policy logit (choice x ep_trial at GO/D2, a model output) gives only +0.01.
